This is DISTINCT from the RC record's negative probe, which DELETED the alias variable and passed the full re-indexed expression at each call site (that measured real 145 at 200 insns); this one KEEPS a single alias variable and moves where it points. Result: the target's `addi r29,r4,204` + `addi r4,r29,0` is now reproduced exactly where ours emitted `addi r29,r4,200` + `addi r4,r29,4` (twice), closing regnorm rows @0x0074, @0x00a4 and @0x012c and dropping genuine STRUCTURAL from 39 to 36.
attributes.residual: swbos stands at real 132, T199/O199, and is RECLASSIFIED: it was carried as a postprocessor-class candidate on the strength of a 6-opcode ops signature; it was 169 differing words, 54 of them absent from the target's word multiset entirely, and reaching real 0 would need at least three unbuilt classes at once -- store fusion (3 words), local-area slot reassignment INCLUDING a one-object-to-two split (30 words), and an FPR-web difference where the target holds a value live in an extra register across ~0x200 bytes (its `fmr f4,f1` at +0x238 and `fmr f4,f2` at +0x2a8 against our two surplus prologue fmrs). Composing those is re-deriving the target's register and stack allocation rather than relating ours to it, which is the class ceiling AGENTS.md draws. THE DOMINANT REMAINING FACT, for whoever takes swbos next: the target names 10 distinct frame slots where our build names 8, and the decisive words are the projection-buffer addresses -- the target emits `addi r6,r1,84` (0x38c10054, T+0x0a8) for the first MBWindowProject call and `addi r6,r1,80` (0x38c10050, T+0x130) for the second, while our build emits the SAME word `addi r6,r1,32` (0x38c10020) at BOTH sites (O+0x0b0 and O+0x138); the paired loads agree (T+0x0b8 0xa8610054, T+0x140 0xa8610050, ours 0xa8610020 twice). The target has two projection buffers where our source has one, reused. That is a SEPARATE fact from the 40-byte local-area base displacement, and the CL record's probe 2 already showed the two-buffer split is reproducible in ARRANGEMENT but regresses on its own while the base is wrong -- and CL/CI/CH between them exhausted the base from source. No hypothesis is mandated here precisely because that pairing is already measured dead; a lane wanting swbos needs a new lever on the BASE, not another buffer probe. ScreenSaverUpdateWeap is not a postprocessor customer either, for an additional independent reason: its frame SIZE differs (target `stwu r1,-216(r1)` against our -200) and its saved-register set differs (`stmw r16,136(r1)` against our `stmw r15,116(r1)`).
